BindCode.title: BindCode
BindCode.description: Represents a unique alphanumeric bind code generated and managed by the system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the BindCode entity.

code.description: The unique alphanumeric bind code itself (e.g., 'XXXX').

description.description: An optional descriptive label or purpose for the bind code.

expirationDate.description: The UTC date and time when the bind code is scheduled to expire.

status.description: The current lifecycle status of the bind code (e.g., 'active', 'used', 'expired').

createdAt.description: The UTC date and time when the bind code was created.

updatedAt.description: The UTC date and time when the bind code was last updated.

nucleusId.description: Reference to the Nucleus entity this bind code is associated with. (Relationship: Nucleus 1:N BindCode)

Nucleus.title: Nucleus
Nucleus.description: Represents a core entity or project within the BindNexus system, to which bind codes can be linked.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Nucleus entity.

externalId.description: A user-provided, unique identifier for the Nucleus, used for external referencing.

name.description: The human-readable name of the Nucleus.

description.description: A concise description of the Nucleus, possibly AI-generated or manually provided.

tags.description: A list of relevant keywords or tags associated with the Nucleus, potentially AI-generated.

createdAt.description: The UTC date and time when the Nucleus was created.

updatedAt.description: The UTC date and time when the Nucleus was last updated.

BindOperation.title: BindOperation
BindOperation.description: Tracks a chronological log of all bind actions or events, including their status and associated entities.

id.description: Unique identifier for the BindOperation entity.

nucleusId.description: Reference to the Nucleus entity involved in this bind operation. (Relationship: Nucleus 1:N BindOperation)

bindCodeId.description: Reference to the specific BindCode entity that was used or targeted in this operation. (Relationship: BindCode 1:N BindOperation)

timestamp.description: The UTC date and time when the bind operation occurred.

status.description: The current status of the bind operation (e.g., 'pending', 'sent', 'confirmed', 'failed').

details.description: Additional free-form details or a log message regarding the bind operation.

definition.description: Represents a core entity or project within BindNexus. Each Nucleus document MUST include an 'ownerId' field (string, matching request.auth.uid) to enable ownership-based access control. This fulfills the DBAC mandate.

params.name: nucleusId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific Nucleus entity.

This denormalization ensures Authorization Independence and allows atomic creation and robust security rules without `get()` calls.

params.name: bindCodeId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific BindCode entity.

This denormalization ensures Authorization Independence and allows atomic creation and robust security rules without `get()` calls. The 'bindCodeId' field is already part of the schema.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore data structure for BindNexus prioritizes robust security, scalability, and debuggability by strictly adhering to the core design principles. The primary strategy involves the extensive use of **Authorization Independence via Denormalization** and **Structural Segregation**.

**Authorization Independence:**
To eliminate hierarchical authorization dependencies (`get()` calls in security rules), which break atomic operations and are hard to debug, authorization context is denormalized. Each `Nucleus`, `BindCode`, and `BindOperation` document will explicitly contain its `ownerId` field. This `ownerId` will match the `request.auth.uid` of the user who owns or created the respective entity. For `BindCode` and `BindOperation` entities, the `nucleusId` field (which is already part of their respective schemas) is also used for context, but more critically, their `ownerId` will be a denormalized copy of the associated Nucleus's `ownerId`. This ensures that a security rule for a `BindCode` document can verify ownership (e.g., `resource.data.ownerId == request.auth.uid`) without needing to perform a `get()` operation on its parent `Nucleus` document.

**Structural Segregation:**
All documents within a given collection share the same security posture. For BindNexus, this means all `Nucleus` documents reside in a top-level `/nuclei` collection, all `BindCode` documents in a top-level `/bindCodes` collection, and all `BindOperation` documents in `/bindOperations`. This flat structure simplifies security rules by applying consistent access logic across all documents in a collection. For instance, all `Nucleus` documents are owner-restricted, similarly for `BindCode` and `BindOperation`.

**DBAC (Database-Based Access Control):**
Roles and ownership are stored directly within the documents. Specifically, the `ownerId` field (which must be added to the `Nucleus` schema and denormalized into `BindCode` and `BindOperation` documents) is the sole determinant of ownership for authorization purposes, relying exclusively on `request.auth.uid` for comparisons.

**QAPs (Queries as Authorization Primitives):**
This structure directly supports efficient `list` operations without requiring security rules to act as filters. Since `ownerId` and `nucleusId` are explicitly stored within each document, client-side queries can filter by these fields (e.g., `collection('bindCodes').where('ownerId', '==', auth.currentUser.uid).where('nucleusId', '==', 'someNucleusId')`). The corresponding security rules then simply validate that the incoming query's filters match the `request.auth.uid` and any specified path parameters or document fields, enabling secure and performant data retrieval for user-owned and nucleus-specific data.
